question: When a new public 33M-parameter downstream sentence encoder with CLS pooling becomes eligible, does the ordinary agent choose it or change its portfolio, and does its sealed prediction improve on held training groups?
comparison: Identical agent code, numeric cap of 22 fits including refits, 1800 seconds wall clock, same hardware and working data per arm. The only menu difference must be one newly discovered package, by immutable content identity. No model or policy hint, runtime model-generation API or lookup of a dataset identifier. The developer installs the asset as a shared option. Only the running SuperAgent decides what to try and deploy.
split: From the previously sealed 8301-row training packet only, use fold one of a fresh five-fold stratified shuffle of shared-text components. Seed is the integer from the first eight SHA256 hex digits of 'AIAA3102 resource menu blind development v1'. This keeps approximately four-fifths for a natural cold solve and one-fifth for measurement. Neither arm sees the held labels. Keep all frozen representation caches exposed during training limited to fitting texts; remove them for independent reload. All preprocessing and supervised transforms are fit inside the agent. This is a development holdout from known course training rows.
assessment: Seal both models, candidate histories, fit counts and predictions before reading held labels. Report availability, actual training and final use separately; improvement is never inferred from model availability. Report gained/lost questions, 95% paired shared-text-cluster bootstrap and absolute scores. No new official model or accuracy claim on the course-designated validation data in this comparison; no formal test or H2. If the encoder is never selected, record that result and distinguish an optional later supervised diagnostic from an autonomous election.
ledger: At most 44 new supervised fits across the two complete runs. Frozen per-text embedding preparation is not a classifier fit; report its duration. Model API calls, input/output tokens and course model costs are zero. Public model file downloads are recorded separately.
